(2) Build the source code Configure the CMake project and build the particarver target: if [ -f "$PC_Z3/bin/libz3.so" ]; then PC_Z3_LIBRARY="$PC_Z3/bin/libz3.so"else PC_Z3_LIBRARY="$PC_Z3/lib/libz3.so"ficmake -S "$PC_ROOT/SVF" -B "$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build" \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \ -DSVF_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON \ -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \ -DLLVM_DIR="$PC_LLVM/lib/cmake/llvm" \ -DLLVM_CLANG="$PC_LLVM/bin/clang" \ -DZ3_DIR="$PC_Z3" \ -DZ3_INCLUDES="$PC_Z3/include" \ -DZ3_LIBRARIES="$PC_Z3_LIBRARY" \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH="$PC_Z3/bin;$PC_Z3/lib"cmake --build "$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build" \ --target particarver --parallel 2 A successful build generates: SVF/PartiCarver-build/bin/particarver PartiCarver executableSVF/PartiCarver-build/lib/extapi.bc SVF external-API analysis model Display the command-line options with: "$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build/bin/particarver" -help (3) Prepare the input PartiCarver takes LLVM bitcode and a JSON security policy. For a single C source file, generate bitcode with the selected Clang installation: "$PC_LLVM/bin/clang" -O0 -g -emit-llvm -c \ /absolute/path/to/program.c -o /absolute/path/to/program.bc For a multi-file program, compile the translation units to bitcode and combine them with the matching llvm-link before analysis. A policy declares components, sensitive values, and pinned functions. For example, a program with a global variable named secret and a function named main can use the following policy, saved as policy.json: { "components": ["Secure", "Public"], "sensitive-values": {"Secure": ["secret"]}, "pinned-functions": {"Secure": ["main"]}, "declassifiers": []} Replace the policy's symbol names with those in your program. The privileged component supplied to PartiCarver must match a component declared in the policy. (4) Run PartiCarver Set absolute paths for the bitcode and policy. Run the native executable from a fresh result directory so its generated files are collected in one place: PC_INPUT=/absolute/path/to/program.bcPC_POLICY=/absolute/path/to/policy.jsonPC_OUTPUT="$PC_ROOT/runs/program-all"mkdir -p "$PC_ROOT/runs"( set -e mkdir -- "$PC_OUTPUT" cd -- "$PC_OUTPUT" "$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build/bin/particarver" \ -dfs -clock-type=wall -stat=false \ -extapi="$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build/lib/extapi.bc" \ -particarver-policy-file="$PC_POLICY" \ -particarver-secure-component=Secure \ -particarver-ptr-params \ -particarver-opt-refine=guided \ -particarver-opt-refine-root-selection=guided \ -particarver-opt-refine-max-rounds=5 \ -particarver-opt-refine-min-gap=1 \ -particarver-opt-refine-time-budget=0 \ -particarver-opt-refine-random-seed=0 \ -particarver-opt-refine-query-mode=all \ "$PC_INPUT" > run.log 2>&1) Choose a different PC_OUTPUT for each run. The example uses guided refinement and at most five nonempty batches. The all query mode selects all currently untried legal roots associated with the selected blockers. For a finite budget, replace -particarver-opt-refine-query-mode=all with -particarver-opt-refine-query-mode=topk and add, for example, -particarver-opt-refine-topk=20. In this configuration, -particarver-ptr-params skips the same-component constraints for pointer-containing arguments and returns. Blocker selection checks each candidate constraint for a violating relaxed-optimal partition at the fixed minimum cost (Equation 8). The final partition is checked against the generated hard constraints for the selected configuration. (5) Inspect the analysis results The example writes its outputs to runs/program-all/. (6) Minimal demo With Python 3.8 or later, run from the project root: python3 Demo/run.py --llvm "$PC_LLVM" --z3 "$PC_Z3" The script builds and runs in a new temporary directory. Expected privileged IR instruction counts are 27 → 21 → 16: Stage 2 removes 6 instructions and Stage 3 removes 5 more. The demo uses k=all and n_max=5; its initial constraints are already satisfiable, so Stage 2's reduction comes from MO. To additionally verify optimality and that consumer can leave Secure only after Stage 3, use the output directory printed by the demo: python3 Demo/check_results.py /path/to/demo-output --z3 "$PC_Z3" Both final partitions must satisfy their full hard constraints. The additional checks report UNSAT for a lower-cost partition at either stage, and UNSAT/SAT for moving consumer outside Secure before/after Stage 3, respectively. title: External Quantum Reservoir Guidance for Complex AI-Assistant Tasks
abstract: External Quantum Reservoir Assist is designed to help an AI assistant identify the core of a difficult request and organize a useful response by adding dynamically generated guidance through a REST or MCP integration. This study evaluates final answers from an archived experiment using one response pair from each of 50 synthetic scenario families. Thirty-nine pairs formed the primary complex decision-support group, while eleven provided routine, constraint-challenge, and technical-explanation controls. Within the primary group, reservoir-assisted answers were preferred in 17 cases, baseline answers in 8, with 13 ties and 1 unclear case. The tie-adjusted preference rate was 61.8% (95% family-bootstrap interval: 48.7–73.7%). The clearest descriptive gains were observed in actionability and validation guidance, while major-error flags occurred equally often in both conditions. Assistance increased total token usage by 32.9% and median paired estimated end-to-end time by 7.51 seconds. The results provide directional evidence that external reservoir guidance can improve practical decision support for selected complex AI-assistant tasks, while also demonstrating substantial uncertainty and operational overhead. The study does not establish general response superiority, reduced factual-error rates, or a quantum-specific advantage. The accompanying minimized dataset and executable analysis reproduce the reported statistics and figures without additional model calls.

title: GHC with stream fusion, used as benchmark in the publication: Higher Order Patterns for Rewrite Rules
abstract: I have added higher order patterns to GHC's rewrite rules which should make stream fusion more viable. So, this dataset contains a development version of the GHC compiler with patches applied to replace the fold/build fusion mechanism with a stream fusion mechanism. I have used this modified version of the GHC compiler to perform the benchmarks in my paper. The benchmarks are performed using Hadrian and on the nofib benchmark suite which is included in the GHC repository.
